claims.text: Introducing controlled coherent nanoprecipitates into RHEAs will increase strength.
Introducing controlled coherent nanoprecipitates into RHEAs will improve tensile ductility.
Introducing controlled coherent nanoprecipitates will maintain high-temperature stability.
Introducing controlled coherent nanoprecipitates will maintain irradiation stability.
The proposed initial material is a nanocrystalline, MoNbTaTiW-based RHEA with a stable solid solution and no significant nanoprecipitates.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation can produce coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy.
The SCCP treatment will produce fine, uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates.
The relevant operating regime includes temperatures of 800 °C and above under heavy-ion or neutron irradiation comparable to fusion-reactor service.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces relieve stress concentrations that could cause premature crack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates strengthen the alloy by obstructing dislocation motion.
The nanoprecipitates will avoid significant coarsening or microstructural degradation at high temperature.
The nanoprecipitates will avoid significant coarsening or microstructural degradation during irradiation.
An SCCP-designed tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy can attain an ambient-temperature strength near 2 GPa and tensile ductility around 15%.
The treated alloy will have both higher tensile strength and higher ductility than the same RHEA processed without controlled nanoprecipitation.
RHEAs processed without nanoprecipitation treatment typically have lower high-temperature strength.
RHEAs processed without nanoprecipitation treatment may suffer irradiation-induced defects or grain refinement.
The benefit will be lost if the nanoprecipitates coarsen or dissolve beyond temperature or irradiation-dose design limits.
